Interface Option<T>

Type Parameters:
T - The type of the values that can potentially be stored in the option
All Known Implementing Classes:
None, Some
public sealed interface Option<T> permits Some<T>, None<T>
Represents a value that may or may not be present. Options are useful for handling data that may or may not be present without risking potential NullPointerExceptions or NoSuchElementExceptions.

This interface is intended to be used with pattern-matching if and switch statements, a Java language feature introduced in Java 21. See the official Java documentation for more information on this language feature. 

// Usage in if statements:
Option<String> potentialText = fetchData(); // Pretend this function exists for sake of example
if (potentialText instanceof Some(String text)) {
  System.out.println("Got text: " + text);
} else {
  System.err.println("Didn't get any text");
}

// Usage in switch statements:
switch (potentialText) {
  case Some(String text) -> System.out.println("Got text: " + text);
  case None() -> System.err.println("Didn't get any text");
}
See Also:

  • Method Details

    • some

      static <T> Option<T> some(T value)
      Creates a new option wrapping a value. An exception is thrown if the value is null. If you want to safely handle values that are possibly null, use ofNullable(Object) instead.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of the values that can potentially be stored in the option
      Parameters:
      value - The value to wrap. Cannot be null.
      Returns:
      An option for the value.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if value is null

    • none

      static <T> None<T> none()
      Creates an empty option containing no data.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of values that could have potentially been stored in the option
      Returns:
      A no-value option

    • ofNullable

      static <T> Option<T> ofNullable(T value)
      Creates an option wrapping a potentially null value. If the value is null, an empty None value is returned, otherwise a Some wrapping the non-null value is returned.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of values that can be stored in the option
      Parameters:
      value - The value to wrap. May be null.
      Returns:
      An option corresponding to the given nullable value

    • ofOptional

      static <T> Option<T> ofOptional(Optional<? extends T> javaOptional)
      Creates a new option corresponding to a java.util.Optional object. If the optional is present, a Some is option is returned; otherwise, a None option is returned.
      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of the values that can potentially be stored in the option.
      Parameters:
      javaOptional - The Java Optional object to wrap. Cannot be null.
      Returns:
      An option for the optional value.

    • filter

      Option<T> filter(Predicate<? super T> predicate)
      Returns an option describing the value of this option if it matches the given predicate. Otherwise, returns an empty option.
      Parameters:
      predicate - The predicate to test the value against. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      An option containing the original value if the predicate is satisfied, or an empty option if the predicate is not satisfied or if this option is empty.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if predicate is null

    • map

      <R> Option<R> map(Function<? super T, ? extends R> mapper)
      Applies a mapping function to the value in this option, returning a new option containing the result of the mapping function. The function may return null; if so, an empty option is returned. Applying a mapping function to an empty option always returns another empty option. This function is equivalent to the following switch statement: 
      Option<?> option = ...;
Option<?> mapped = switch (option) {
  case Some(var value) -> Option.of(mappingFunction.apply(value));
  case None() -> Option.none();
};
      Type Parameters:
      R - The result type of the mapping function
      Parameters:
      mapper - The mapping function to apply.
      Returns:
      An option containing the result of the mapping operation, or an empty option if the mapping function returned null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if mapper is null

    • flatMap

      <R> Option<R> flatMap(Function<? super T, ? extends Option<? extends R>> mapper)
      Like map(Function), but where the function may return another Option object instead of a raw value. Useful to avoid stackups of nested Option<Option<Option<...>>> types.
      Type Parameters:
      R - The result type of the mapping function
      Parameters:
      mapper - The mapping function to apply
      Returns:
      An option containing the result of the mapping operation

    • stream

      Stream<T> stream()
      If a value is present, returns a sequential Stream containing only that value, otherwise returns an empty Stream.

      This method can be used to transform a Stream of option elements to a Stream of present value elements: 

      Stream<Option<T>> os = ..
Stream<T> s = os.flatMap(Option::stream)
      Returns:
      the optional value as a Stream
